story: Thursday afternoon in Sumter Oaks is hazy and humid at 81 degrees, and Gary is hopeful as he tells Hal he'll keep his cart in the garage until the review notice clears it for the street. Hal, wary about whether Gary's modifications need Architectural Review under Code L-01, is glad to hear it, while Rosa heads to Town Hall with Gary's sketches under her arm. Over at the Rec Center, Donna, looking determined, studies the ladder standings board to see who the team needs to beat.
events: Donna (ladder standings board): Study the ladder standings to see who we need to beat

gary.thought_process: I just read the Architectural Review notice on the bulletin board and Hal has shown up. Rosa left for Town Square, and my memory says she was taking my sketches to the review desk, so I shouldn't pester anyone twice about it. Hal asked about the cart before, and I owe him a plain update. Parade is Saturday, so I want to keep things moving and be honest about where the cart stands: no mods on the street until approval comes through, since L-01 covers exterior changes. I can tell him I read the notice and that the wiring work can go forward inside the garage in the meantime.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Hal. Just read the review notice on the board. Nothing's cleared for the street yet, so I'll keep the cart in the garage and do the wiring work in there until it is. Rosa's carrying my sketches over to the desk.

donna.thought_process: I'm at the Rec Center with nobody around, and my goal is getting Gary ready as my doubles partner for the ladder climb. Gary is off reading his Architectural Review notice, so I can't talk to him right now. Rather than stand around, I'll check the ladder standings board to see exactly where Pruitt-Kowalski sit and what we need to climb. That gives me concrete info to bring to Gary when he shows up.

parameters.content: Study the ladder standings to see who we need to beat

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with the binoculars notebook ready and Gary is right here in line-of-sight. I haven't seen his cart sketches in person, and I told myself a neighbor deserves a straight word before the committee hears about it. L-01 requires Architectural Review approval for visible cart modifications. A direct question is fair and by the book, and if he has no approval, he'll know what's coming at tomorrow's meeting. Gruff but not cruel.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Gary. Those modifications on your cart, they go through Architectural Review? Code L-01 says they have to, and the committee meets tomorrow.

rosa.thought_process: I just got to Town Square and nobody's around. Gary's at the bulletin board reading the Review notice on his cart application, and Donna went off to the Rec Center. The Architectural Review desk is at Town Hall, which connects from here, and I'm carrying Gary's clamp list and light layout folder for the Thursday walk. Best move is to head to Town Hall, get the folder in front of Review, and be ready when Gary and Donna catch up. No one's here to talk to, so no point lingering.

parameters.content: Heading to Town Hall with Gary's folder so we can lay out the tuck-on cart plan for Architectural Review.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
